## Synthesis Overview

PR #127 extracts the Phase 7f critique/revision loop from `story-orchestrator` into a dedicated `quality-reviewer` subagent. All three models agree the PR is not ready to merge, but they diverge substantially on which defects are most critical: Claude focused on the SKILL.md companion-file gap and a decision-matrix edge case; GPT focused on runtime-blocking tool contract defects and a missing critique mode; Gemini identified the broadest finding set, confirming both categories. Four of the five highest-severity findings were confirmed by direct tool-code inspection during synthesis. No finding achieved all-three consensus, but every Critical finding was independently corroborated by either two models, by tool code, or both.

**Model Agreement Score:** 4/10 — Each model pair agrees on a different subset of findings; no finding was unanimously reported, and each model has a distinct critical focus. Claude missed the two most severe runtime defects; GPT missed the companion-file gap; Gemini's coverage was the broadest.

### ★★☆ Majority Findings (Two of Three Models Agree)

#### [M-C-01] Unsupported `parse-scores` contract — Phase 7f loop fails on first iteration

```
Severity: Critical
Category: Correctness
File: .opencode/agents/quality-reviewer.md
Lines: 58–68
Models: Claude ✗  GPT ✓  Gemini ✓
Verified: Yes — critique_runner.py lines 409–411 confirm the error messages produced

Detail: Step 2b instructs the subagent to call critique-runner with
operation: "parse-scores", name, and iteration, intending to retrieve an aggregate
score. The actual parse-scores operation (critique_runner.py:237) requires
--critic-type and --response-text to parse a raw LLM response string; it does not
support reading aggregate results from a savepoint and has no name or iteration
parameters. The tool will immediately exit with "--critic-type required for
parse-scores" or "--response-text required for parse-scores" (exit code 2), making
the entire Phase 7f quality-review loop non-functional from the very first iteration.
The should-refine operation in Step 2c already returns overall_average directly —
the parse-scores step is both broken and redundant.

Suggestion: Remove Step 2b entirely. In Step 2c (should-refine), capture the
returned overall_average field as current_score. Use that value for best-score
comparison and tracking.
```

---

#### [M-C-02] `story-pipeline/SKILL.md` contains false constraint blocking quality-reviewer dispatch

```
Severity: Critical
Category: Correctness
File: .opencode/skills/story-pipeline/SKILL.md
Lines: 149, 158
Models: Claude ✓  GPT ✗  Gemini ✓
Verified: Yes — grep confirms both lines still read "four subagents" / "only four"

Detail: Line 149 states "The pipeline uses four subagents" and line 158 contains the
hard constraint "These are the only four subagents the orchestrator may dispatch."
Both are now incorrect. Any orchestrator session that loads this skill will receive
an authoritative false statement that quality-reviewer cannot be dispatched and will
not find it in the reference table. This is a live contradiction in a skill the
orchestrator is expected to load, not merely stale documentation.

Note: GPT reviewed only four files and did not check SKILL.md. This finding would
very likely have been unanimous had all reviewers inspected it.

Suggestion: Update line 149 to "five subagents". Add quality-reviewer to the
subagent reference table with: "Run the Phase 7f critique/revision loop for a
single chapter | Phase 7f". Update line 158 to "These are the only five subagents
the orchestrator may dispatch."
```

#### [M-C-03] Best-scoring chapter text never stored — revision-cap fallback returns wrong draft

```
Severity: Critical  (synthesized — Gemini: Critical, GPT: Warning)
Category: Correctness
File: .opencode/agents/quality-reviewer.md
Lines: 38–115
Models: Claude ✗  GPT ✓  Gemini ✓
Verified: Yes — grep confirms best_chapter_text does not appear anywhere in the file

Detail: The workflow initialises best_score and updates it when a higher-scoring
revision appears, but never stores the chapter text associated with that score.
Only current_chapter_text (the latest revision) is maintained. When the revision
cap is exhausted with the final draft scoring lower than an earlier iteration —
e.g., iteration 3 scores 75 after iteration 2 scored 80 — the agent returns the
lower-scoring latest draft as accepted_chapter_text. This directly contradicts the
documented guarantee in story-orchestrator.md and docs/features/story-orchestrator.md:
"When a quality gate fails after maximum revision attempts, the best-scoring version
is accepted." GPT classified this as Warning; Gemini as Critical. Given the explicit
architectural promise in the feature documentation, Critical is the more appropriate
severity for this synthesis.

Suggestion: Initialise best_chapter_text = provided chapter_text at Step 1
alongside best_score. In the scoring comparison at Step 2c/2d, whenever a new score
exceeds best_score, update both: best_score = current_score and
best_chapter_text = current_chapter_text. In Step 3, return best_chapter_text as
accepted_chapter_text, not current_chapter_text.
```

#### [M-W-01] Decision matrix undefined for misconfigured `chapter_min_revisions > chapter_max_revisions`

```
Severity: Warning
Category: Correctness
File: .opencode/agents/quality-reviewer.md
Lines: 72–80
Models: Claude ✓  GPT ✗  Gemini ✓

Detail: The four-row decision matrix does not cover the case where
chapter_min_revisions > chapter_max_revisions (e.g., min = 3, max = 1). In this
configuration, when should_refine is false and revision_count < min, Row 2 requires
revision_count < chapter_max_revisions to force a revision — but at or above cap,
that condition is false. Row 4 handles the >= max case only for should_refine = true.
No row covers the intersection of should_refine = false AND < min AND >= max
simultaneously. The LLM has no defined branch to follow and may hallucinate a path,
stall, or loop.

Suggestion: Add a catch-all fallback row: any | any | >= chapter_max_revisions →
Accept — max revisions reached (cap overrides min). Alternatively, add a pre-flight
guard in Step 1 that validates chapter_min_revisions ≤ chapter_max_revisions and
fails fast with a clear error if the configuration is invalid.
```

### ★☆☆ Singular Findings (Only One Model Reported)

---

#### [S-C-01] All `critique-runner` calls omit `mode: "chapter"` — entire loop evaluates wrong artifact type

```
Severity: Critical
Category: Correctness
File: .opencode/agents/quality-reviewer.md
Lines: 56–75, 87–90
Model: GPT
Verified: Yes — critique_runner.py line 366 confirms default="outline"; grep on
quality-reviewer.md confirms no occurrence of mode: "chapter" anywhere in the file

Detail: GPT reported that critique-runner defaults to outline mode and every
invocation in the new subagent omits mode: "chapter". Tool-code inspection
independently confirms this: critique_runner.py argument parser sets
default="outline" for --mode (line 366), and the quality-reviewer agent file
contains no instance of mode: "chapter". Every critique-runner call in the Phase 7f
loop — run-critics, should-refine, generate-feedback — will therefore operate on
the outline critic set, use the outline savepoint namespace, and evaluate the wrong
artifact type, breaking the core purpose of the extracted subagent.

Assessment: Confirmed by direct tool-code inspection. Although only GPT raised this
finding, it is verified and Critical. Claude and Gemini appear to have missed it.

Suggestion: Add mode: "chapter" to every critique-runner invocation in the agent
workflow: run-critics (Step 2a), should-refine (Step 2c), generate-feedback (Step 2f),
and any replacement for the removed parse-scores step.
```

---

#### [S-W-01] `savepoint-mgr` save call missing required `data` parameter

```
Severity: Warning
Category: Correctness
File: .opencode/agents/quality-reviewer.md
Lines: 95–96
Model: Gemini
Verified: Yes — savepoint_manager.py line 166 prints "Error: --data is required for
save" when --data is absent

Detail: Step 2g instructs the subagent to call savepoint-mgr to write the quality
revision savepoint, but does not specify what value to pass for the data parameter.
The savepoint_manager.py argument parser documents --data as "required for save"
(line 157) and enforces it at line 166 with an error exit. The save call as written
will fail, and no savepoint will be recorded for the quality revision.

Suggestion: Update Step 2g to explicitly pass data: current_chapter_text (or the
JSON-serialised revision payload if the savepoint convention expects structured data).
```

---

#### [S-I-01] Savepoint name uses "/" separator — inconsistent with all other project savepoints

```
Severity: Suggestion
Category: Style
File: .opencode/agents/quality-reviewer.md
Lines: 101
Model: Claude

Detail: The quality revision savepoint is named chapter_{N}/quality_revision_{revision_count},
using "/" as a hierarchical separator. Every other savepoint in the project uses
underscore separators (init, outline_complete, characters_complete,
chapter_{N}_complete). Depending on how savepoint-mgr stores keys internally,
the "/" may create nested filesystem paths, collide with the platform path separator,
or simply make savepoints harder to discover.

Assessment: Low-priority style issue, straightforward to fix.

Suggestion: Rename to chapter_{N}_quality_revision_{revision_count} (e.g.,
chapter_3_quality_revision_1) to match the established convention.
```

## Summary

All three models agree the branch is not ready to merge. The quality-reviewer subagent, as written, cannot complete a single iteration of the Phase 7f loop: the parse-scores step (item 1) will error on first call, and the tool defaults (item 2) mean critics would evaluate the wrong artifact type even if that step were skipped. Items 3 and 4 are pre-merge correctness requirements. Items 5 and 6 are lower-severity but tool-verified defects. Item 7 is a low-priority style cleanup.

**Confirmed Critical defects requiring fix before merge: 4** (items 1–4)
**Confirmed Critical defect requiring fix before merge: 1** (item 2, singular but tool-verified)
**Total findings requiring action: 6** (items 1–6)
**Deferred: 1** (item 7)
